messages:
meera: Heads up — saw a sustained throughput drop on us-east-1 dedicated yesterday at ~22:10 UTC. Traffic stayed steady but worker restarts and GPU OOMs spiked. Not sure if this is kernel-routing churn or KV cache thrash.
alan: copying logs now. Any recent deploys to runtime or kernel heuristics?
meera: small config tweak to kernel-routing heuristics rolled at 21:55 (canary -> prod). Also a low-level allocator tweak from last week.
sara: alert from perf-alerts: `throughput_drop >= 30% for 10m, worker_restarts++`, linked span: https://internal/perf/17777 (redacted). Pushing pprof snapshots to /tmp/profiles/177777.
jorge: can you paste the worker stderr tail? especially allocator and kvcache eviction lines.
meera: tail: ```
[2026-02-11T22:09:53Z] ERROR worker-17: GPU OOM when servicing request id=abc123, alloc 12.3GiB > limit 12.0GiB
[2026-02-11T22:09:54Z] WARN kvcache: evicting prefix 'chat:session:' size=46MB -> freed 12MiB
[2026-02-11T22:09:54Z] INFO kernel-router: selected kernel v2.1 for seq=2048, latency_est=32ms
[2026-02-11T22:09:55Z] ERROR worker-17: restarting after OOM
```
alan: kvcache frees are tiny relative to the requested allocation — looks like fragmentation. Are we seeing slab splits?
sara: pprof shows high cudamalloc retries and many small free calls after prefix eviction. Stack traces point to kernel v2.1 allocation path.
meera: interesting — the fallback policy was configured to attempt kernel v2.1 then v1.9 on failure; v2.1 has a slightly higher peak working set but better throughput. If many requests get routed to v2.1 concurrently, memory pressure could spike.
jorge: noisy neighbor possibility: any single tenant with large context windows around that time? Querying tenant logs...
meera: tenant 'media-inc' had a 2m burst of long-context infer (seq length ~4096) at 22:08. It aligns with OOM window.
alan: that could push kernel v2.1 allocations above threshold. Suggest immediate mitigation: update routing to prefer v1.9 for non-critical tiers (10% shift) and increase batch timeout for v2.1 to reduce concurrency.
sara: rolled a quick canary to prefer v1.9 for standard tier at 22:30 — canary on 5% nodes. Initial metrics: worker restarts down from 12/min -> 4/min. Throughput recovering slowly.
meera: good. For postmortem: we need to understand memory fragmentation pattern — whether per-request allocations cause slab blowup or evictions are just too small to free contiguous pages.
jorge: captured allocator histograms: many 4KiB-64KiB free ops, but large allocations fail due to no contiguous region. Looks like external fragmentation.
alan: two follow-ups: 1) add a proactive coalescing sweep during low-util windows (experiment), 2) compute routing cost that includes fragmentation risk: avoid v2.1 when free_contiguous < X.
sara: also saw kernel-selection thrash: controller re-routed inflight requests mid-seq after failed allocations which triggered extra retries and doubled KV cache churn. Will add rate-limit on mid-sequence kernel-switching.
meera: agreed. Action items: 
- meera: write incident blameless summary and timeline (T+6h).
- alan: prototype fragmentation-aware routing rule and a canary config (T+24h).
- sara: collect full pprof heap + cudamalloc traces and upload to perf bucket (T+12h).
- jorge: evaluate coalescing sweep risk on staging with heavy long-context load (T+48h).

oncall-bot: Incident alert cleared at 23:05 UTC — throughput within 5% of baseline and restarts <= 1/min for 15m.
meera: reassigning to runtime perf squad for root-cause and mitigation PRs. Thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:
alan: logging follow-up PRs in #eng-runtime backlog.
jorge: posting a short repro harness for long-context bursts to /tools/repro/kvfrag. Please run before any allocator change.
sara: saving traces and profiles to https://perfstore/internal/177777-profile.tar.gz (access: runtime-perf).
meera: closing thread for now — will reopen if anomalies reappear after the infra changes.
